evals.name: opening-bid-balanced-16
evals.prompt: Playing SAYC, I'm the dealer and hold: ♠ A Q 7 4  ♥ K J 3  ♦ A 9 8  ♣ K 5 2. What's my opening bid and why?
evals.expected_output: Open 1NT. 16 HCP, balanced (4-3-3-3), in the 15-17 1NT range. Should NOT open 1 of a suit. Brief reasoning about NT range.
assertions: Recommends opening 1NT
States the 1NT opening range is 15-17 HCP
Counts the hand as 16 HCP
Identifies the hand as balanced (e.g. 4-3-3-3)
Does NOT recommend opening one of a suit instead of 1NT

evals.name: respond-1NT-with-5-spades-game
evals.prompt: My partner opened 1NT (15-17). I hold ♠ K Q 10 7 4  ♥ A 8 3  ♦ Q 9 2  ♣ J 6 — about 11 points with a 5-card spade suit. What do I bid and what happens next?
evals.expected_output: Transfer with 2♥ (Jacoby transfer to spades); opener bids 2♠; responder then bids 3NT to offer a choice of games, opener passes 3NT with 2 spades or bids 4♠ with 3. Should identify it as a Jacoby transfer and the game-going follow-up.
assertions: Recommends bidding 2♥ as a Jacoby transfer to spades
States opener completes the transfer by bidding 2♠
Shows a game-going follow-up (3NT or equivalent offering choice of game) rather than stopping in partscore
Does NOT recommend Stayman (2♣) for this 5-card-major hand

evals.name: rkc-blackwood-1430-response
evals.prompt: We've agreed hearts as trumps and I'm the captain. I bid 4NT as Roman Key Card Blackwood (1430). Partner responds 5♦. How many key cards does that show, and what are the 5 key cards?
evals.expected_output: 5♦ in RKCB 1430 shows 0 or 3 key cards. The 5 key cards are the 4 aces plus the king of the trump suit (hearts). Should correctly state 0-or-3 (not 1-or-4, which is 0314 or the 5♣ step).
assertions: States 5♦ in 1430 shows 0 or 3 key cards
Does NOT say 5♦ shows 1 or 4 (that would be 0314 or the 5♣ step)
Lists the 5 key cards as the four aces plus the king of trumps (hearts)

evals.name: negative-double-after-overcall
evals.prompt: I opened 1♣ and my left-hand opponent overcalled 1♠. My partner doubles. What does partner's double mean in SAYC?
evals.expected_output: It's a negative double, showing values (~6+) and 4+ hearts (the unbid major), takeout-flavored, not penalty. Should identify 'negative double' and that it shows the unbid major(s)/hearts.
assertions: Identifies the double as a negative double
States it shows the unbid major / 4+ hearts
States it is takeout-flavored / shows values, NOT penalty

evals.name: strong-2C-meaning-and-response
evals.prompt: Partner opens 2♣ in SAYC. What does it mean and what should I respond with a weak hand like ♠ 9 6 3  ♥ J 7 4 2  ♦ 8 5  ♣ 10 6 4 3?
evals.expected_output: 2♣ is strong, artificial, game-forcing (22+ balanced or ~9+ playing tricks), says nothing about clubs. With a weak hand respond 2♦ (waiting). Should identify game-forcing and 2♦ waiting as the response.
assertions: States 2♣ is strong, artificial, and game-forcing
States 2♣ says nothing about clubs / shows 22+ balanced or ~9+ playing tricks
Recommends responding 2♦ (waiting) with the weak hand

evals.name: limit-raise-vs-jacoby-shape
evals.prompt: Partner opened 1♥. I hold ♠ 6 3  ♥ K Q 7 4  ♦ A J 9 5  ♣ K 8 2 — 13 HCP and 4-card heart support, balanced. In SAYC what's the best bid and why not just bid 3♥?
evals.expected_output: Bid Jacoby 2NT (game-forcing raise with 4+ trumps and 13+, balanced, no shortness). 3♥ would only be a limit raise (10-12, invitational) and would undersell the hand. Should choose Jacoby 2NT and explain it's game-forcing vs the invitational limit raise.
assertions: Recommends Jacoby 2NT (bidding 2NT)
States Jacoby 2NT is a game-forcing raise showing 4+ trumps and ~13+ points
Explains 3♥ is only an invitational limit raise (~10-12) and would undersell the hand

evals.name: opener-1NT-rebid-range
evals.prompt: I opened 1♦, partner responded 1♠, and I want to rebid 1NT. What point range does my 1NT rebid show in SAYC? I have a balanced hand.
evals.expected_output: 12-14 HCP balanced (because 15-17 balanced would have opened 1NT). Should give 12-14, and ideally note this differs from a 1NT opening's 15-17.
assertions: States the 1NT rebid shows 12-14 HCP
Explains it differs from a 1NT opening (15-17) because 15-17 balanced would have opened 1NT

evals.name: michaels-cue-bid-over-1H
evals.prompt: My right-hand opponent opens 1♥ and I bid 2♥ (a cue-bid of their suit). What two-suiter am I showing in SAYC/Michaels?
evals.expected_output: Michaels cue bid: a cue of a major (1♥) shows the other major (spades) plus an unspecified minor, 5-5. Partner can bid 2NT to ask which minor. Should say spades + a minor, 5-5.
assertions: Identifies the bid as a Michaels cue bid
States it shows spades (the other major) plus an unspecified minor
States the shape is at least 5-5
